name: TraversalComponentServerFacet_SyncIsAutoTraversalEnabled
summary: The client tells the traversal server facet whether auto-traversal is on. A 45-byte record with a 17-byte body: the shared head then ONE strict boolean byte, read by the same shared bool reader FUN_1425a3070 that five of these small setting messages use.
purpose: Carry the client's auto-traversal setting to the traversal component. What the server does with it is not measured.

created_when: the traversal component pushes its auto-traversal setting
lifecycle.if_absent: the server never learns the client's auto-traversal setting

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): typed header 00 01 b0 42, i.e. type index 4272 = 0x10b0. A client record carries the body at record offset 28: the 8-byte frame head and the 16-byte actor id precede the typed header, so a 17-byte body makes a 45-byte record.

fields.name: local_facet_id
fields.note: Measured 28 8c 27 b1 a6 be 71 cc = 0x288c27b1a6be71cc. First u64 of the shared message head: the sending facet's own local id. The traversal client facet's own id.
fields.provenance: corpus-wide scan; the head's first u64 is named in msg.time-sync-to-client.json from FUN_1416c1c40

fields.name: local_actor_id_word0
fields.note: Measured bf 85 31 4b bc 4a 95 1a = 0xbf85314bbc4a951a, the first 8 bytes of the client's own actor id - the same value every other capture carries.
fields.provenance: already earned in msg.time-sync-to-client.json; re-measured here

fields.name: enabled_flag
fields.note: Measured 0x00, leaving nothing over: 16 + 1 = 17 exactly. The reader writes the object's +0x20 byte as a single strict non-zero test and its decode side FUN_1425a30b0 rejects any byte at or above 2, so the width and the strictness are both from the codec. What the flag SWITCHES is not measured: only the value 0 was captured, so the field is named for the on/off setting the message name announces, not for an observed behaviour.
